bearings.paper_claim: Single-feature voice-trait correlations of about 0.30 to 0.48 in Sample 1 (n=78) did not replicate in Sample 2 (n=44, self-report only): the top features differed, and the authors say the results did not coincide. They note two different microphones may have contributed to this, alongside noise, colds and fatigue. Voice alone reached about 60 percent best-case three-class accuracy against over 75 percent for facial-expression work, and they call personality prediction multimodal.

bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper gives no effect-size estimate for channel instability. Its own wording is that microphones may have contributed, alongside other factors, so the defensible claim is that feature-level findings did not replicate across two samples recorded on different microphones. The claim that a channel change can wipe out findings overstates the paper. Cite the venue numbers from the brain ladder with their source, since the brain also gives a 21.8 per 1k live median.
bearings.verifier_note: Numbers in Section 3.1 and Table 4 match the paper. The paper says microphones may have contributed, not that the authors blame the switch. The rel cites brain line 44 for a claim that line does not contain.

bearings.paper_claim: Top-five-feature random forest, leave-one-out on N=100, three classes at training 25th and 75th percentiles. All-cases accuracy: self-report N 50, E 46, O 46, A 53, C 43 percent; expert N 57, E 60, O 57, A 56, C 53; close others N 54, E 57, O 45, A 52, C 54. Chance is 33 percent; a constant central-class predictor gets 50 percent (p.14). The paper does not say whether feature selection ran inside each fold, and reports no multiple-comparison correction across 1941 features.

bearings.system_side: Audio pilot ridge uses all 88 features with GridSearch inside each outer fold, repeated 5-fold CV over 5 seeds, and a 40-draw permutation null printed as diagnostic (b5_audio_eval.py). The brain says b5_audio_eval composites are mis-signed and superseded by b5_es_crossmodal.py, which uses 5000 label permutations. The +0.208 held-out r was recorded and then superseded the same day as gender-confounded (brain topic note, locked robustness look 34bf7e4). The perm p=.0002 figure could not be verified.

bearings.transfer_conditions: Rubio accuracies are not a bar or prior for Melange looks. Self-report cells mostly sit at or below the 50 percent central-class baseline, but Agreeableness at 53 is above it, so do not say none exceed it. The Melange N look used n=110 (brain: r -0.0016, perm-p .511), not n=90. Do not present the superseded +0.208 as current evidence.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers in Table 6 match exactly. The rel's self-report claim is wrong for Agreeableness (53 above 50). The rel's N=90 contradicts the brain's n=110. The rel omits that +0.208 was superseded as gender-confounded. The cited b5_audio_eval composite is the one the brain says not to trust for sign.

summary_issues: The paper says N=100 but its two samples are 78 and 44, which sum to 122. The rel summary reports this correctly.
Rel summary says self-report accuracy is no better than the 50 percent baseline. Agreeableness at 53 exceeds 50, so the claim is slightly wrong.
Rel summary says a microphone change can wipe out feature findings. The paper says only that microphones may have contributed; this overstates it.
Rel summary says the audio N MISS was at N=90. The brain records the consumed N look at n=110 (r -0.0016, perm-p .511).
Rel summary gives held-out r=+0.208 at the Melange N as a live ES re-test. The brain says it was superseded the same day as gender-confounded (locked robustness look 34bf7e4).

The paul_alignment paragraph cites Paul's notes and a Ramey quote about contextual or auditory constraints. The item has no Paul entries and no annotation hashes (paul_entries empty, annot_sha12s empty), and the same paragraph says Paul did not annotate this paper. Unsupported; strike it.
The discussion says expert extraversion correlates with volume variation at -0.50, which is not in Table 4 (expert E is 0.48). The rel does not mention this internal inconsistency.

Discussion correlations (N 0.38, E 0.40) contradict the Results (E 0.47 self, 0.48 expert), and the text says all correlations p<0.001 with a maximum of 0.50 while Table 4 shows p values of 0.004 to 0.008 and a maximum of 0.48. The rel reports these correctly.
Ext says recruitment was paid extra credit. The paper says students register for extra course credit; nothing says they were paid.

Ext says three-class accuracy beats chance for most criteria. All 15 all-cases cells exceed 33 percent (lowest 43), so the accurate statement is all of them. Ext also says Expert Extraversion 60 percent is the best prediction cell; it is the best all-cases cell, while Expert Neuroticism medium-trait accuracy at 81.1 is the highest single cell.

Ext attributes the claim that audio predicts self-report and expert traits in AVIs to Koutsoumpis (ref 49) alone. The paper cites refs 49 and 50 together for that sentence. Ext's 'about 10 percent' for Marrero is verified; the 'Speaker Personality Corpus' description for Mohammadi and Vinciarelli is not in the paper.
